_readme: THE SCREEN REGISTER — [pipeline C-13] company/pipeline/02-shared-chassis.md
The complete set of NON-APP-SPECIFIC screens: the ones that are the same in all fifty apps and
therefore ship in the chassis rather than being written per app. Sourced from DoD §4-A.
WHY A REGISTER AND NOT A CHECKLIST IN PROSE. C-13's acceptance is that a NAMED LIST is declared and
the app_brick probe asserts each screen is present in a fresh stamp. A list nobody can check is how
an account-deletion button sat doing nothing for months while passing every check the repo had.
STATUS values:
present  - it exists in the chassis; `anchor` names the file and the symbol that prove it
blocked  - it CANNOT be built yet; `blockedBy` names what has to land first, and that claim is
checked (a blocker that has already shipped fails the build, so nothing hides behind
a stale excuse)
todo     - buildable now, not yet built. Counted and PRINTED on every run.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-screen-set.mjs.
ANCHOR KINDS. `anchor.kind` says what the symbol IS, because a bare word match is the
declaration-vs-usage trap: renaming `class NotFoundScreen` to `class NotFoundScreenGone` left the
guard green, since the class's own constructor still matched the bare name.
class  (default) - our own widget/class; matches the DECLARATION
member           - a method we own
uses             - a Flutter widget we use rather than declare (SegmentedButton, AboutListTile)
STATUS `not-building` — a fourth state, added 2026-07-29. It means: this screen was CONSIDERED and
deliberately not built, with the reason recorded. It is not `todo` (nobody is coming back to it) and
not `blocked` (nothing is in the way). Every entry names why building it would produce a DEAD
FEATURE — a language picker with one locale, a profile form that saves nowhere — which is the shape
[2]C-6 exists to catch. A deliberate no is worth more than a permanent todo.
⚠️ A SUPERSEDED `todo` IS THE ONE DRIFT THIS GUARD CANNOT CATCH GENERICALLY. `firstrun.screens` sat
here as a todo after both of its halves had been split out into `firstrun.permission-priming`
(present) and `firstrun.splash-onboarding` (not-building) — a stale entry that read as outstanding
work. Nothing mechanical distinguishes it from a real todo, so WHEN YOU SPLIT AN ENTRY, DELETE THE
ORIGINAL in the same edit. Found 2026-07-29 by reading the list, not by running it.
🔴 THREE ENTRIES WERE MOVED BACK FROM `not-building` TO `todo` ON 2026-07-29, after the owner asked
what was actually blocking them. Each original reason stated a SYMPTOM as a CAUSE — "no profile data
model", "content is app-specific", "no users to ask" — and none survived checking. The language
picker was the fourth and is now built. THE RULE: a `not-building` entry must name what would
un-block it, and that un-blocker must be genuinely hard. If it is one file, it is a todo.

screens.what: A friendly screen when a widget throws during build, instead of Flutter's grey/red default.

reachable.why: installed before runApp, so an error in the FIRST build is already covered

screens.what: 404 for a route that does not resolve. Matters most on web, where a user can type a URL or follow a stale link.

reachable.why: without it go_router shows its own error page, which names internal route patterns

screens.what: Tells the user the network could not be reached. Driven by a FAILED REQUEST, not a connectivity plugin — knowing the radio is on says nothing about whether the API is reachable.
The kill-switch wall when the running version is below min_supported_version.

reachable.why: mounted in MaterialApp's builder, above the router

screens.what: The DPDP analytics consent question. THE single piece that turns the whole analytics rail on.

reachable.why: [2]C-6: the recorder had ZERO call sites and every event was silently discarded, and no test went red because refusing is the correct behaviour when consent is absent

screens.what: The settings screen itself.

reachable.why: a screen no route reaches is one no user can open

screens.what: Light/dark/system choice, persisted.
Opens a support email with the app name pre-filled.
Delete the account and its data, with re-authentication first.

reachable.why: its confirm button called Navigator.pop and NOTHING else until 2026-07-28 — a store-compliance defect that passed every check the repo had

screens.what: Standard about dialog with version and legalese.
The paywall shell.
screens.detail: PaywallGate exists in the design system with ZERO consumers. Wiring it before a payment can be taken would be a fail-closed seam with no proven open path — the [2]C-6 shape. Kept as a shell deliberately.

screens.what: In-progress / success / error / manage-subscription.
screens.detail: Nothing can be purchased yet, so every one of these would be a screen no path reaches.

screens.what: Sign-in, sign-up and forgot-password, plus the redirect guard that gates every other route.

reachable.why: the REDIRECT GUARD is what makes these screens reachable — screens do not navigate after sign-in themselves, because pushing from both places leaves two routes racing to be top of the stack. 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-07-29: that was true about getting IN and false about getting OUT. `redirect` re-runs when the router is TOLD to, and nothing watched `authStateChanges()`, so a stamped app signed the user in and went on showing them the form they had just completed. This pattern matched throughout — PRESENCE IS NOT ENFORCEMENT, and no single grep can prove a screen can be left. The exit is proven instead by the `auth-redirect-follows-session` property, which drives the real form; found by running it, not by reading it.

screens.what: Password reset, email verification and the OAuth callback — the screens a link outside the app lands on.
screens.detail: Each of these is entered by following a link from an EMAIL or a browser redirect, so none can be reached without deep-link handling. `app_links` 7.2.1 supports all six platforms (verified against pub.dev 2026-07-28) and would earn its place under [2]C-4 as native-binary — it ships platform code — but it is not a dependency yet. ⚠️ Web carries two traps recorded in AuthCapabilities: the token arrives in the URL FRAGMENT so query parsing fails SILENTLY, and app_links on web reports only the INITIAL link.

screens.what: Ends the session on this device.

reachable.why: placed ABOVE account deletion — it is the action a user wants hundreds of times more often, and putting the irreversible one first invites a misfire

screens.what: Reminder toggle, gated on what the platform can actually do.

reachable.why: [2]C-7 earning its keep in real UI: on Linux the plugin shows but cannot schedule, and on Windows (pinned 17.x) it does neither. An honest sentence replaces the toggle there, because a switch that silently does nothing is worse than no switch

screens.what: Privacy policy and terms of service, reachable in-app.

reachable.why: both stores require these to be reachable IN-APP, not only from a store listing

screens.what: Explains why a permission is wanted BEFORE the OS prompt appears.

reachable.why: the OS prompt can be shown ONCE on most platforms — a user who declines it has effectively declined permanently, so the cost of asking at a bad moment is the feature, forever. Declining the PRIMING deliberately does not spend the OS prompt

screens.what: Edit display name.

reachable.why: BUILT 2026-07-29, after being refused on "there is no profile data model" — which described a field nothing wrote and concluded it could never be written. gotrue's `updateUser` writes `auth.users.user_metadata`, and the adapter now writes the SAME `full_name` key it already read. The tile watches the identity STREAM rather than the `currentUser` snapshot: a snapshot read compiles, renders, and never rebuilds, so a saved name would go on showing the old value — which is what a save button wired to nothing looks like

screens.what: Language picker, with "follow the device" as a real option.

reachable.why: MaterialApp must READ the override, or the picker stores a choice the app ignores. Was recorded as not-building on 2026-07-29 ("only one locale exists") — which stated the symptom as the cause: nothing blocked adding a second ARB, and the i18n seam had never once run

screens.what: Onboarding carousel. (The SPLASH half is correctly not-building — see detail.)
screens.detail: RE-OPENED 2026-07-29, the onboarding half only. Was not-building on "content is app-specific" — WRONG for the mechanism: `AppConfig.copy` is a runtime copy-override map that already exists, so a carousel can be CONFIG-DRIVEN rather than fabricated. The chassis owns the carousel, each app owns its words. ⚠️ The SPLASH half stands and is not re-opened: a splash is native platform configuration (launch storyboard / drawable), not a Flutter screen — a Dart one renders AFTER the native splash and adds a second flash.

screens.what: Ask for a store review at a good moment.

reachable.why: BUILT 2026-07-29. The refusal was "no users to ask" — an argument about WHEN, not about whether the mechanism can be built, and WHEN turned out to be pure arithmetic over four persisted numbers (`core.ReviewGate`). ⚠️ THE CALL SITE IS THE WHOLE POINT: the gate refuses on almost every launch BY DESIGN, so "nothing happened" is the correct outcome nearly always and a seam with no caller would be invisible for the life of the app. This is the [2]C-6 shape with the best possible camouflage. The prompt itself is OS-drawn and unobservable — neither store reports whether anything appeared — so what is proven is that the request ARRIVES once the gate agrees
